headline: All seven majors remain below their 200-day lines; whales move coins to cold storage while stablecoin float shrinks and shorts get liquidated.
paragraphs: The regime is underwater across the board. Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, Ripple, Binance Coin, Dogecoin, and Cardano are all trading below their 200-day simple moving averages, and no golden cross exists among them. The entire major cap index is below the intermediate trend line. Bitcoin sits 48.8% below its 12-month high of $124,739.81, while Ethereum is down 61.2% from $4,817.76, and Solana sits 70.2% below $247.60. Cardano has traveled the farthest, down 80% from its year peak. This is not a mild correction; it is a structural bear regime where the long-term trend is confirmed below in every asset the desk tracks.

Momentum offers a quiet divergence worth noting. Bitcoin's RSI-14 stands at 49.5 (neutral) and its MACD is below signal, matching the downtrend. Ethereum's RSI is 51.5 (neutral) and MACD is also below signal. Most of the group follows suit: Solana at RSI 46, XRP at 45.2, Dogecoin at 43, all with MACD below. But Binance Coin shows RSI 57.6 with MACD above signal, and Cardano sits at a striking RSI of 67 with MACD above signal, despite trading below its 200-day line. This is the tape saying that while the majority is resting or weakening in a downtrend, two assets are generating short-term upward momentum even as they remain structurally impaired. Cardano's RSI above 67 specifically signals overbought conditions in a bear regime, a fragile state.

Derivatives positioning reveals crowded longs and sharp short liquidations. Bitcoin's funding rate stands at 0.01% per 8 hours (11% annualized), meaning longs are paying to hold their positions; the long-short ratio is 1.64, so longs outnumber shorts but not by an extreme margin. Open interest is $2.02 billion. Over the last 24 hours, shorts absorbed $6.12 million in liquidations while longs took only $1.36 million, a five-to-one imbalance. Ethereum shows the same pattern: annualized funding at 1.3% (lower than Bitcoin, suggesting less heat), long-short ratio of 1.97, but $7.22 million in short liquidations against $2.14 million in long liquidations over 24 hours. Solana's funding at 0.01% per 8 hours (11% annualized) with a long-short ratio of 2.67 and shorts losing $636,604 to longs' $116,722 in liquidations. Across the board, shorts are being wrung out while the long side remains the crowded trade, and funding rates are elevated enough to be paying for that crowding.

Whale flows show coins moving away from trading venues and into cold storage or private wallets. Over the last 24 hours, $287.2 million net moved off exchanges, with Bitcoin accounting for $233.4 million of that outflow (inflows of $145.8 million, outflows of $379.2 million) and Ethereum adding $53.8 million off-exchange. The biggest moves off-venue were $174.8 million in USDT from OKEx, $120 million in USDC from Coinbase Institutional, and $114.3 million in Bitcoin from Kraken. Meanwhile, the biggest deposits onto exchanges were USDC and USDT flowing into Coinbase Institutional and Bitfinex, totaling roughly $240 million. The pattern is mixed but skewed: whales are hoarding Bitcoin and Ethereum in self-custody while stablecoins are rotating into institutional exchange infrastructure. Stablecoin total float stands at $305.8 billion, down 0.88% over 30 days, so dry powder is not accumulating. The weekly net flow over the last four weeks shows a recent reversal: negative outflows of $313 million and $239 million two weeks ago, then positive inflows of $1.12 billion and $1.20 billion in the two most recent weeks, suggesting recent accumulation.

Spot ETF flows show a divergence. Bitcoin ETF inflows on 03 Aug 2026 were $170.1 million, with a five-session net of $120.2 million positive. Ethereum ETF recorded outflows of $11.9 million on the same date, with a five-session net of $13.6 million negative. Only one day of same-direction behavior in each asset, so no persistence claim is valid, but the direction differs: Bitcoin is receiving traditional finance demand while Ethereum is not. The sentiment gauge reads Extreme Fear at 25, on a 30-day range of 20 to 33, so fear is near its lowest point in the recent window. This creates a classic tape contradiction: the crowd is extremely afraid, the derivative shorts are being liquidated on rallies, long positioning is crowded and funding is positive, yet whales are hoarding coins off exchange and Bitcoin spot ETFs are receiving flows while the entire major cap index remains structurally below the 200-day line.

What to watch: Bitcoin and Ethereum reclaiming their 200-day moving averages would confirm a regime change. A reversal in whale flows, with coins moving back onto exchanges, would signal late accumulation rather than early. A sustained flip in funding rate from positive to negative would tell you the longs are no longer willing to pay, a sign of positioning exhaustion. For now, the tape shows extreme fear coexisting with elevated long funding and off-exchange accumulation, which is the posture of early-stage recovery rather than capitulation, but the structural trend remains in place until the 200-day line is reclaimed.
